ei.title: 서논술형 Practice1 (Ch4): Musical Training & the Brain / Mug Texture & Taste
ei.subject: 올림포스 영어독해 기본1

fullPassage: There is no question that learning to sing or play a musical instrument changes the structure of your brain. If you enjoy music but have no special training, then your brain processes it mostly through its right hemisphere, the side of the brain that deals with emotion. In the face of music, you are 'right-lateralised'. Many studies show that musical training shifts the brain's processing of music to its left hemisphere; musicians are left-brained. There are several guesses about why this happens. One explanation is that they have learned to hear music more like language, discerning a level of structural complexity beyond the grasp of ordinary listeners. When trained musicians hear music, it activates the part of the brain associated with language comprehension. A group of researchers at the University of Twente in the Netherlands recently 3D-printed two identically shaped mugs with different textures to test the effects on taste. One was covered in a rounded bobbly texture, and the other had a blocky, angular texture. In a supermarket taste test for a fictitious new brand made by the study team, the researchers offered shoppers a sample of coffee from one of the mugs and asked them to evaluate the taste for qualities including sweetness, bitterness, intensity and pleasantness. Drinks in the round bobbly mug tasted on average around 18 percent sweeter, while in the angular-textured mug the same drinks tasted up to 27 percent more bitter and much more intense. If you're trying to cut down on your sugar, avoid drinking from a mug with a rough or angular texture — go for a round bowl and mug, and if possible ones with a smooth rounded texture too.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: If you have no special training, your brain processes it mostly through its right hemisphere, the side of the brain that deals with emotion.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 훈련 없으면 감정 담당 우뇌로 처리 ←정답
❌ ② 훈련된 음악가가 우뇌로 — 훈련되면 '좌뇌'로 이동
❌ ③ 모양이 다른 컵 — 모양은 같고(identically shaped) 질감만 다름
❌ ④ 둥근 컵이 더 쓰다 — 둥근 컵은 더 '달게' 느껴짐
det.tip: no special training → right hemisphere (emotion)

ch: 특별한 훈련이 없으면 음악은 주로 감정을 담당하는 우뇌로 처리된다.
훈련된 음악가는 음악을 주로 우뇌를 통해 처리한다.
연구진은 서로 모양이 다른 두 개의 머그컵을 사용했다.
둥근 컵의 음료가 각진 컵의 음료보다 더 쓰게 느껴졌다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: two identically shaped mugs with different textures / a fictitious new brand
det.analysis:
❌ ① 변화를 주지 않는다 — 본문은 뇌 구조를 '바꾼다'

✅(일치) ④ 거친/각진 컵 피하기 — 본문 일치

둥근 오돌토돌한 컵의 음료는 평균 약 18% 더 달게 느껴졌다.

questions.passage: There is no question that learning to sing or play a musical instrument changes the structure of your brain. If you enjoy music but have no special training, then your brain processes it mostly through its right hemisphere, the side of the brain that deals with emotion. In the face of music, you are 'right-lateralised'. Many studies show that musical training shifts the brain's processing of music to its left hemisphere; musicians are left-brained. There are several guesses about why this happens. One explanation is that they have learned to hear music more like language, discerning a level of structural complexity beyond the grasp of ordinary listeners. When trained musicians hear music, it activates the part of the brain associated with language comprehension. A group of researchers at the University of Twente in the Netherlands recently 3D-printed two identically shaped mugs with different textures to test the effects on taste. One was covered in a rounded bobbly texture, and the other had a blocky, angular texture. In a supermarket taste test for a fictitious new brand made by the study team, the researchers offered shoppers a sample of coffee from one of the mugs and asked them to evaluate the taste for qualities including sweetness, bitterness, intensity and pleasantness. Drinks in the round bobbly mug tasted on average around 18 percent sweeter, while in the angular-textured mug the same drinks tasted up to 27 percent more bitter and much more intense. If you're trying to cut down on your sugar, avoid drinking from a mug with a rough or angular texture — go for a round bowl and mug, and if possible ones with a smooth rounded texture too.
